issues.description:
[bug-hunt] After scaling a meal's portion (e.g. Half), the recipe page shows the ORIGINAL full-size quantities - the calorie-target renormalizer overwrites the user's saved portion scale, and tapping Save persists the undo.

EXPECTED: a saved portion scale (UserMealModification written by POST /diet/log-modification {scale:0.5}) renders as saved everywhere; the target-kcal safety net should only normalize the pristine recipe expansion, never user-authored modifications.
ACTUAL: RecipeDetailResource builds ingredients from the user's modification (backend.py:7038-7053), then unconditionally applies the target-kcal renormalizer (backend.py:7077-7096): after a 0.5x scale, current_kcal is ~50% of meal.calories_kcal, deviation >5%, so every quantity+macro is rescaled x2 - right back to full size. Meanwhile the nutrition card (daily diet GET) uses the halved quantities directly, so the two screens contradict each other. If the user believes the recipe screen and taps "Save Meal Changes", the re-inflated quantities are persisted and their portion choice is silently destroyed.

REPRO: Nutrition -> meal -> portion sheet -> scale to Half (card macros halve, correct) -> tap meal -> Recipe -> ingredient quantities + header macros are back at FULL size (wrong) -> tap "Save Meal Changes" -> nutrition card jumps back to full portions.

WHERE: backend.py RecipeDetailResource ~7077 (renormalizer has no "user modification present" guard). FIX: skip target-kcal rescaling when ingredients_data came from a UserMealModification.
issues.reviewReason: FIXED in backend: RecipeDetailResource now sets from_modification=True when ingredients_data comes from a UserMealModification, and skips calorie renormalization when from_modification is True (backend.py line 7083). Confirmed deployed on prod via grep.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Users who were away 14-60 days are forced to re-login (OTP) even though their refresh token is still valid for up to 60 days - the "refresh expired token at startup" path is dead code.

EXPECTED: on app open with an expired access token but a stored refresh token, the app attempts POST /auth/refresh (backend refresh tokens live 60 days - JWT_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRES=timedelta(days=60), backend.py:215, and the endpoint needs only refresh_token in the body). Only if THAT fails should the user land on the login screen.
ACTUAL: authService.isAuthenticated() (src/services/auth.service.ts ~334) returns false for an expired access token with the comment "Don't trigger refresh here - let checkAuth handle it" - but AuthContext.checkAuth (src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx ~57-86) only calls checkAndRefreshToken() INSIDE the "if (authenticated)" branch. When authenticated=false the else branch just clears the user. So the isExpired -> refreshToken(true) branch inside checkAndRefreshToken (auth.service.ts ~291) is unreachable from cold start, and a user idle >14 days is dumped to Welcome and must re-do email OTP despite holding a perfectly refreshable session. The 14-day access expiry (TOKEN_EXPIRY_DURATION, src/lib/api-config.ts:36) vs 60-day refresh window makes this a real user-facing logout for anyone returning after a 2-8 week break - exactly the lapsed users the app wants back frictionlessly.

REPRO (dev): 1) Login normally. 2) In devtools set nyus_token_expiry to Date.now()-1000 (simulates >14 days idle; refresh token untouched and still valid). 3) Reload the app. Observed: instant redirect to Welcome/login, no POST /auth/refresh in the network tab. Expected: silent refresh, user stays logged in.

WHERE: src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx checkAuth (refresh call gated on authenticated===true) + src/services/auth.service.ts isAuthenticated/checkAndRefreshToken. FIX: in checkAuth, when isAuthenticated() is false but a refresh token exists, await authService.refreshToken(true) and re-evaluate before rendering the logged-out state.

issues.description:
[suggestion] Coach speaks your language: a "Coach language" preference (English / Hinglish / हिन्दी) that makes AI coach chat replies and weekly insights come back in the user's chosen language.

USER PROBLEM: NYUS is India-focused, but the AI coach — the product's centerpiece and the premium tier's main selling point — replies only in English. Many Indian users think and type in Hinglish ("aaj do roti aur dal khaya, kitna protein hua?"); the model understands them fine but always answers in formal English, which reads distant and drops less-fluent users out of the chat habit entirely. Competitor parity: HealthifyMe's Ria coach supports Hindi + regional languages and markets that hard.

EVIDENCE: zero language/locale preference exists anywhere in the frontend (grep for hindi/hinglish/preferred_language/i18n across src = no product matches); coach prompts in llm_prompts.py are English-only. Users already CAN write Hinglish to the coach today — we just never reply in kind, so the gap is purely one missing preference + one prompt line.

PROPOSED V1: (1) "Coach language" row in Profile preferences (English / Hinglish / Hindi), saved as a user pref; (2) inject one line into the coach-chat + weekly-insights system prompts: "Reply in <lang>; keep numbers, food names, and exercise names unchanged"; (3) scope = /coach-chat messages + weekly insight text ONLY — app UI stays English (no i18n project), and plan wizards stay English in v1 (their inline option-extraction regexes assume English structure).

EFFORT: small — ~1 day full-stack: one Profile preferences row, one backend pref column (or prefs JSON key), one prompt injection point. Purely additive; trivial to remove if it underwhelms.
issues.reviewReason: Owner reply noted: 'do this on the entire application'. Coach-language v1 (chat + weekly insights in English/Hinglish/Hindi) is SHIPPED and live. Full-app languages = translating every screen (300+ strings across ~60 pages) + locale plumbing; i18n scaffolding already exists in src/i18n. PLAN (phased, next ticks): P1 wire i18next provider + persist language from the existing Coach-language pref; P2 translate core daily loop (dashboard/nutrition/activity/profile/notifications); P3 onboarding + plan wizards; P4 remaining surfaces + QA pass per language. Each phase ships behind the same pref so partial coverage never mixes languages mid-screen (untranslated keys fall back to English). Starting P1 next tick unless you want a different language set or scope.
